scenes.headline: The Supreme Being
visual: The tree, the soul, and the Supreme
scenes.say: Chapter Fifteen. The Supreme Being. Krishna describes the world as a great tree, and then shows what lies beyond it.
Imagine a tree turned upside down. Verse one. {verse}

scenes.headline: Cut the tree
visual: Nourished by the three gunas
Sense pleasures are its sprouts
Cut its roots with the axe of detachment
scenes.say: Its branches spread through the whole cosmos, nourished by the three modes of nature, with sense pleasures as its sprouts. Its true form cannot be seen from here, nor its beginning, nor its end. But its firm roots, ego and desire, can be cut, Krishna says, with the strong axe of detachment and knowledge. Then one seeks the place from which there is no return.
Who reaches that place? Verse five. {verse}
Then Krishna says something intimate about every one of us. Verse seven. {verse}
And he describes what happens at death with an image as light as a breeze. Verse eight. {verse}

scenes.headline: The light in the sun, the fire within
visual: The light of the sun, the moon and fire
The energy that holds up the earth
The fire that digests our food
scenes.say: And where is God in all of this? Everywhere life is sustained. The light of the sun that lights the world, and the light in the moon and in fire, is his. Entering the earth, he supports all beings. As the moon, he nourishes the plants. As the fire of digestion in every body, he turns our food into life.
Finally, Krishna names three levels of reality, and places himself above them. Verse eighteen. {verse}

visual: Rooted above in the Supreme
Branching down into the world
Cut its roots: ego, attachment, desire
scenes.say: Lesson one. The world is a tree of Maya; cut it with self-knowledge. Creation is like an upside-down banyan, rooted above in the Supreme and branching down into the world. Its roots are ego, attachment and desire. Cut them with knowledge and detachment, and you are free.

visual: The soul carries the senses and the mind
From body to body
As the wind carries a fragrance
scenes.say: Lesson two. The soul carries its impressions from body to body. As the wind carries a fragrance from a flower, the soul carries the senses and the mind into its next body. The ignorant cannot see this. Those with the eye of knowledge can.

visual: The light of the sun, the moon and fire
The nourishment in the plants, the fire within
Memory and knowledge come from Him
scenes.say: Lesson three. God is the inner light and sustainer of all life. The light of the sun, the moon and fire is his. He nourishes the plants and digests our food. He sits in every heart, and from him come memory, knowledge and the clearing of doubt.

scenes.headline: Three levels of being
visual: Temporal beings
The eternal soul
The Supreme Being
scenes.say: Lesson four. Three entities: temporal beings, the eternal soul, and the Supreme. All created things change and pass. The individual soul does not change. And the Supreme Being, God, is beyond both, sustaining and pervading them. Whoever knows this, knows everything.

scenes.headline: Cut the roots, find the source
visual: The world is a tree rooted in God
The soul moves on like a fragrance
God is the light in all, and beyond all
scenes.say: So, Chapter Fifteen. The world is a great tree whose roots reach up to God, and the axe of detachment cuts us free. The soul moves from body to body like a fragrance on the wind. And God is the light in everything, and beyond everything. Next, Krishna describes two kinds of people.
